full_judgment: 5. In the instant case, it is not disputed that the accused persons of the G. R. Case took the defence that Ambia Khatun was in possession on the basis of purchase. However, the accused persons were convicted under section 448 B.P.C: but the High Court in Criminal Revision No. 141 of 1970 set aside the order of conviction of the accused persons. The judgment in Crl. Revision No. 141 of 1970 does not show any express finding about possession by Ambia Khatun. The accused persons appear to have been acquitted on 6 grounds firstly, that there was no finding in the judgment of the learned Magistrate regarding the intention of the accused. Secondly, the investigating officer was not examined, thirdly, the complainant did not mention the names of the accused Fakir Ahmed and Nur Khatun in the petition of complaint which was over-looked by the Trial Court. Fourthly, the accused persons were not properly examined under section 342 Cr.P.C. fifthly, the trial court did not consider whether the Vendors of Ambia Khatun inherited the property and sixthly, the Trial Court did not consider whether Ambia Khatun herself was in possession of the disputed properly. In the judgment it has also been observed that P. W. 3 Idris Miah admitted in his cross examination as follows: "Ambia is still in the house—" and P. W. 2 Raja Mia admitted in his cross-examination that he and his wife were staying in his father's house. Apart from these observations, there is no finding in the judgment if plea of the accused that Ambia was in possession was true. The witnesses in the case were examined after commission of the alleged offence, and, as such, the statements of the witnesses referred to above cannot be taken as conclusive proof to show possession of Ambia Khatun at the time of commission of the alleged offence. The judgment of the trial Court shows that there was documentary evidence on the side of the complainant C. P. No. 1. The complainant's case was that the disputed. land stands recorded in the name of Abdul Bari, Abdul Jalil (the 2 sons of Darbesh Ali), Hakiman Nessa (mother of Abdul Jalil, Abdul Bari) and Amirun Nessa. Abdul Bari died without leaving behind any issue. Abdul Jalil purchased the share of Amirun Nessa. Subsequently, Abdul Jalil took re-settlement of the disputed land. One Shajada Begum who was P. W. 7 in the C. R. Case was adopted by Abdul Jalil as a daughter and Abdul Jalil gifted the disputed homestead in favour of Shajeda Begum. The complainant put in evidence the R. S. Khatian, the Hibbanama, the kabala executed by Amirun Nessa in favour of Abdul Jalil etc. The defence took the plea that after death of the 2 sons of Darbesh Ali his daughter Safian Nessa's two daughters namely Ajaban Nessa and Aman Nessa and son Moftan Hossain got the homestead by inheritance and sold the same to Ambia Khatun.
